purpose: Adds four guarded pluggable overrides (wp_cache_get/set(_multiple)_salted) to the Redis object-cache drop-in plus a stub-based PHPUnit test file, intended to give WP 6.9+ a native 'salt-in-key' performance optimization.
riskRationale: The shipped code is behaviorally safe and correct: it stores a wrapper array('data','salt') at the stable cache key exactly as WP core's cache-compat.php does, so there is no functional or security regression and memory stays bounded. Risk is limited to (a) a misleading PR description that claims a salt-in-key performance optimization the code does not deliver, (b) an entirely redundant 1:1 re-implementation of core's cache-compat.php fallback that adds drift surface for zero benefit in a performance-critical drop-in, and (c) a new test file that the repo's PHPUnit harness cannot actually discover or execute.

text: The implementation is a faithful, correct copy of WP 6.9's cache-compat.php wrapper-at-stable-key semantics, so it introduces no bugs and no memory/AWS issue - but it also delivers none of the 'salt-in-key / native Redis ops / eliminate wrapper encode-decode + salt comparison' benefit the PR description and title claim. The overrides are behavior-neutral duplicates of core's own fallbacks and add future drift risk; the added PHP test file cannot be discovered by the repo's PHPUnit 11 setup (it runs zero tests). This PR needs a maintainer decision (drop the redundant overrides entirely) and an honest description before merge.

reasoning: Functionally correct but the PR fails to deliver its stated purpose: the overrides are byte-for-byte-equivalent re-implementations of WP core's 6.9 cache-compat.php (same array('data','salt') wrapper at the stable key, same PHP salt comparison on every read), providing zero performance gain on both WP 6.9+ (where core's identical guarded compat function would win anyway) and WP < 6.9 (where these functions are never called). The new test file also cannot execute under the repo's PHPUnit 11 harness (filename/class name mismatch, default suffix not matched), so it provides no coverage. Recommend removing the four overrides, letting core's cache-compat.php run unmodified as the reference redis-cache plugin does, and rewriting the description.

message: The PR description misrepresents the implementation. It claims the drop-in 'embeds the salt directly into the Redis key and stores raw data, eliminating core's wrapper-array (data/salt) encode/decode + PHP salt comparison on every read' via $cache_key.':'.$salt (the 'salt-in-key' Option A). The actual code stores array('data'=>...,'salt'=>...) at the original $cache_key and performs the exact same $salt !== $cache['salt'] comparison on every read (lines 936-1036) - identical to WP core's cache-compat.php. The stated performance optimization is therefore not delivered, the narrative is misleading, and several open review threads were written against the unmerged salt-in-key version. This is why the branch's own autofix iteration (commit 71552fc7) already reverted these functions.
suggestion: Rewrite the PR description and title to match reality: the change adopts core's wrapper-at-stable-key format and provides zero performance gain over core. Then resolve the central decision - drop these redundant overrides entirely (core's cache-compat.php supplies identical behavior for WP 6.9+) or keep them explicitly as version-gated compat shims only - and close the stale threads that reference the salt-in-key design.

message: The four added functions are behavior-neutral re-implementations of WP core's wp_cache_get_salted / wp_cache_set_salted / wp_cache_get_multiple_salted / wp_cache_set_multiple_salted from wp-includes/cache-compat.php (same isset( $cache['salt'], $cache['data'] ) gate, same $salt !== $cache['salt'] comparison, same array('data','salt') wrapper). They change nothing versus core: on WP 6.9+ the drop-in's guarded globals load first and win over core's identical guarded compat functions (no behavioral or perf delta); on WP < 6.9 these functions are never invoked by core (WP_Query/Term_Query only call the salted API in 6.9+), so they are dead code. Net effect: dead code on <6.9, redundant duplicate on 6.9+, and future drift surface if core evolves this contract. The reference redis-cache plugin correctly does not override these at all.
suggestion: Prefer not to ship redundant overrides of cache-compat.php. Remove the four functions and let core's pluggable fallbacks run unmodified. If a decision is made to keep them as explicit WP<6.9 compat shims, state that rationale in a comment and adjust the PR description accordingly.

message: The new PHP test file cannot be executed by the project's test harness, so the claimed coverage is illusory. The class is named ObjectCacheTest but the file is class-object-cache-test.php: PHPUnit 11 requires the basename to match the class name, so invoking it directly fails with 'Class class-object-cache-test cannot be found'. More broadly, phpunit.xml.dist scans the tests/php directory without a custom suffix, so only files matching the default *Test.php / .phpt patterns are collected - 'class-object-cache-test.php' is not, and I confirmed the whole suite currently reports 'No tests executed!'. The PR description's 'npm test (18 suites / 217 tests)' are Jest JS tests and do not exercise this file. The test is therefore neither discoverable by CI nor runnable directly.
suggestion: Rename the file to ObjectCacheTest.php so the class name matches the filename, and confirm the testsuite's <directory> suffix config (or the autoload) actually discovers it; then run composer test and confirm the new tests execute and pass. Wire PHPUnit execution (composer test) into the CI/verification flow so this coverage is real rather than dead.

message: The earlier open review threads written against the salt-in-key design (2026-08-02) are stale against the shipped code. (1) 'unbounded orphaned-key accumulation' - applies only to embedding the salt in the key; the shipped wrapper-at-stable-key design overwrites a single key per write so memory stays bounded. (2) 'non-salted wp_cache_delete cannot invalidate' - also salt-in-key-scoped; the shipped code stores at the original key so plain delete still works (the test_unsalted_delete_invalidates_salted_entry test confirms this). (3) 'no tests cover the new functions' - addressed by the added test file. These threads should be closed/marked not-applicable to avoid confusion; note the remaining concern that the new test file cannot be executed by the harness (see the important issue on the test file).
suggestion: Close or explicitly mark the three 08-02 threads as 'not applicable to the merged wrapper-at-stable-key implementation', and annotate that each was scoped to the abandoned salt-in-key design described in the PR text rather than the shipped code.

message: The signatures strictly match WP 6.9 core - ( $cache_key, $group, $salt ) for getters and ( $cache_key, $data, $group, $salt, $expire = 0 ) for setters - correctly framing the swapped-order signatures in issue #503 that would have broken every WP_Query/WP_Term_Query call site. Array-salt normalization with is_array()? implode( ':', $salt ) matches core's join contract, and expire is cast (int), so on the narrow WP 6.9 path the behavior is a faithful drop-in of the fallback the plugin is copying.

The get_multiple_salted / set_multiple_salted functions correctly remap stored keys back to the original cache keys, preserving core's return contracts (assoc array keyed by original key; false on missing or stale; bool[] on writes), and reject non-array/non-wrapper values gracefully rather than leaking the wrapper array to callers.

Beyond discovery, the test file's assertion set over-covers details that are pure copies of core (exact wrapper shape, non-salted-delete invalidation) while simultaneously having no cross-version coverage (no test for a WP < 6.9 environment where the salted functions are absent - the dead-code path). If the overrides are kept, this matters little; if they are to be dropped, these tests become dead code. The value of the suite depends on the outcome of the core decision.
suggestion: If keeping the functions, add a test proving pre-6.9 behavior is unchanged (functions not present / never called) and drive the array-salt order check from core's real multi-value salt (posts+terms). If dropping, remove the test file along with the overrides.
